CHANGELOG

What changed in MESA

The changes that matter in each MESA Core release, including what to check before upgrading and what is still limited.

Follow with RSSProject status

MESA is alpha software and is not yet recommended for production use.

24 November 2026 Latest

v0.9.5

Versioned documents with point-in-time search, a persistent BM25 index, faster local search on large stores and resumable uploads. The graph store is removed and the package installs on Python 3.14.

Improved

  • Upload each version of a document with metadata.valid_from and search with valid_at. Validity order, not upload order, decides the active version, and intervals are half-open. Results carry revision_number, valid_from and valid_to.
  • In the four-law Turkish temporal fixture, the correct version ranked first on all 18 dated and all 8 undated questions.
  • In a local run with 100,820 chunks on one 8 vCPU machine, the warm models-off HTTP search median fell from 1,223 ms to 753 ms and the deterministic vector lane median was 287 ms.
  • Interrupted whole-document uploads resume from their saved chunks with the chunking plan chosen at admission.

Before you upgrade

  • Take an offline backup first. A forward-only migration clears old graph bookkeeping rows; going back needs v0.9.4 and the pre-upgrade snapshot.
  • The Kùzu graph store is removed. Old kuzu_db files are ignored and can be deleted by hand; graph settings are ignored with a startup warning.
  • LanceDB is locked to 0.41.0; startup adds scope keys to older vector tables.

Known limits

  • The scale figures are local measurements on repeated copies of one corpus; they do not measure retrieval quality at that size. No 0.9.5 benchmark is published yet.
  • Per-minute and daily rate limits are still not enforced for /v4/* and /control/*.

Full technical changelog

23 November 2026

v0.9.4

Search gets simpler defaults and repeatable ranking, whole-document uploads finish sooner, and legacy V3 and LLM consolidation code is removed.

Improved

  • On the shared Tier M DEV store with models and reranking off, passage Hit@5 rose from 50/112 to 61/112, MRR from 0.3411 to 0.3955, and median search latency fell from 361.3 ms to 233.9 ms.
  • A 5 MB models-off document became fully ready in 172.61 s instead of 249.99 s.
  • Two fresh stores built from the same corpus now produce identical ranks.

Before you upgrade

  • Take an offline backup first. Two forward-only migrations remove the V3 node store and routing telemetry; going back needs v0.9.3 and the pre-upgrade snapshot.
  • The graph is now off and the assertion weight is 0.0. Set MESA_GRAPH_ENABLED=true and MESA_RRF_ASSERTION_WEIGHT=1.0 to restore the earlier fusion.
  • V3 routes and clients, LLM consolidation and Tier 3 modes 1/2 are removed. Retired settings are ignored with a startup warning.

Known limits

  • The search figures are DEV results with models off. No 0.9.4 benchmark is published yet, and the 0.9.3 benchmark does not describe this release.
  • Per-minute and daily rate limits are still not enforced for /v4/* and /control/*.

Full technical changelog

16 November 2026

v0.9.3

Large documents become ready much faster, the default embedding model changes, and Turkish search handles uppercase text better.

Improved

  • A 4,999,000-byte document became fully ready in 245.20 s instead of 718.27 s (2.93× faster), measured with models off and graph on.
  • Legal extraction skips impossible reference scans. CPU time for the API-limit TCK/1 input fell from 129.861 ms to 52.330 ms with identical outputs.
  • The default embedding model is now local:BAAI/bge-m3 with 1024 dimensions. Models remain off by default.

Fixed

  • Turkish legal comparisons and date lookups handle uppercase İ and I consistently, so YARGITAY and yargıtay find the same text.
  • MCP sessions now work on a fresh store by creating missing workspace and dataset entries.
  • Startup now fails with a clear error for invalid consolidation settings.

Before you upgrade

  • Stores created with the old default must keep MESA_EMBEDDING_MODEL=local:magibu/embeddingmagibu-200m and MESA_EMBEDDING_DIMENSION=768, or be rebuilt.

Known limits

  • Per-minute and daily rate limits are not enforced for /v4/* and /control/*.
  • ASCII yargitay still does not match Yargıtay.

Full technical changelogBenchmark 0.9.3

6 November 2026

v0.9.2

Legal search understands citations and decision references, and heavy requests no longer stall the service.

New

  • New chunks keep versioned rule items for citations, decision references, dates, amounts, durations and outcomes, with offsets into the original text.
  • An exact law and article, or a decision’s own reference, can take up to three leading result positions.

Improved

  • Document admission briefly waits for queue capacity without repeating the full chunk plan.

Fixed

  • Request-path stalls affecting 0.9.1 are fixed, keeping /health responsive in the measured heavy cases. Upgrading is recommended.

Before you upgrade

  • Set MESA_LEGAL_RULES_ENABLED=false to turn off the new legal rules. Generic retrieval stays available.

Known limits

  • Heavy queries did not become faster: a 1,000-candidate search still took about 11.6 seconds.

Full technical changelogBenchmark 0.9.2

1 November 2026

v0.9.1

Search ranking is retuned, optional reranking arrives, and the CLI waits until documents are ready.

New

  • MESA_CHUNKING=auto|plain selects how documents are split.
  • Optional BGE reranking loads only when it is used.
  • Documents can be deleted by source.

Improved

  • Vector weight moves to 8.0. On the Turkish Round 14 DEV set with reranking off, passage MRR rose from 0.3953 to 0.5663.
  • The CLI waits for ACTIVE by default. Use --no-wait to return at admission.
  • A four-scope cache and ingestion indexes reduce bookkeeping work.

Before you upgrade

  • The Python SDK’s Mesa.add still defaults to wait=False. Pass wait=True to wait for readiness.

Known limits

  • The ranking results are corpus-specific development measurements, not test-split evidence.

Full technical changelog

28 October 2026

v0.9.0

MESA can run locally for one user, with a CLI, a Python SDK and lossless document ingestion.

New

  • Local CLI with start, add, search, delete, status and mcp-config commands.
  • Python SDK Mesa client with zero-config local defaults.
  • Lossless document ingestion through POST /v4/documents, with duplicate detection and revision tracking.
  • MESA_GRAPH_ENABLED=false allows lightweight operation without KùzuDB.

Improved

  • Document purge fully erases stored source and assertion text while keeping audit state and hashes.

Fixed

  • Retry and dead-letter fixes stop records from hanging in RETRY_PENDING.
  • The chunker handles Turkish abbreviations and list numbering without splitting mid-citation.
